lesson: In should_retry, allow retries only for 5xx status codes and 429; all other 4xx errors must be treated as permanent failures and not retried.
why: Retrying 401s previously locked user accounts, while 429 must remain retryable because the upstream service rate-limits in bursts and would otherwise cause dropped work.
quote: should_retry allows 5xx and 429 only, at most 4 attempts, backoff sleeps capped at 60 seconds.

lesson: Configure the retry policy to allow a maximum of four total attempts with exponential backoff sleeps capped at 60 seconds.
why: It defines the bounded retry limits agreed upon to handle transient failures without unbounded delays.
quote: Four attempts total, and cap the exponential backoff at 60 seconds.

lesson: In the retry policy, retryable status codes must include any 5xx response plus specifically 429 and 408 from the 4xx range, while all other 4xx codes fail fast.
why: The upstream edge times out slow requests with 408s that succeed on a second attempt.
quote: 408 joins the retryable set: any 5xx, plus exactly 429 and 408 from the 4xx range. Everything else in 4xx still fails fast.

lesson: The retry backoff ceiling must be capped at 30 seconds, superseding the rejected 60-second ceiling.
why: The gateway load balancer kills idle connections at 32 seconds, which terminated backoff waits under the old 60-second cap.
quote: backoff now caps at 30 seconds (under the LB's 32s idle kill), superseding the old 60-second cap.
